objective: Replace the production FakeRateLimiter(allowed=True) with a real per-user post rate limiter that counts the author's own posts in a sliding window with one indexed query on posts, with limits from Settings, so one signed-in account can no longer publish without bound.
acceptance_criteria: With the default limits (10 per minute, 100 per hour), an author with 9 posts created in the last minute can publish one more, and an author with 10 posts created in the last minute is refused.
An author with 99 posts created in the last hour, none of them in the last minute, can publish one more; an author with 100 posts created in the last hour is refused.

The windows slide and are measured against the database clock: a post created 59 seconds before now() counts against the minute limit and one created 61 seconds before does not; a post created 3599 seconds before now() counts against the hour limit and one created 3601 seconds before does not.
Only the author's own posts count: any number of posts by other authors never refuses this author.
Every kind of post counts and every kind is limited: originals, replies, quote reposts, and plain reposts, including those made through POST /posts/{post_id}/repost.
A refused post answers HTTP 429 with a detail on both POST /posts and POST /posts/{post_id}/repost, persists nothing and publishes no event. Every other moderation refusal keeps answering 400.
The limits come from Settings as POST_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE and POST_RATE_LIMIT_PER_HOUR, defaulting to 10 and 100; zero, a negative number or a non-integer makes Settings construction fail.
One rate-limit check issues exactly one SQL statement (a test counts statements with before_cursor_execute).
An Alembic revision adds an index on posts (author_id, created_at); it upgrades and downgrades cleanly against a real Postgres, as the existing migration tests do.

get_moderation_chain wires the real limiter, in the same fixed chain position (ProfanityFilter -> SpamScoreCheck -> RateLimitCheck -> DuplicateContentCheck); the chain it builds contains no FakeRateLimiter.
backend/openapi.json and frontend/src/api/schema.d.ts match the backend.
